title: Maine Department of Education Annual Summit
before:
ElevatED 2026

About ElevatED

Registration is now open for the summer 2026 ElevatED professional learning experience! Through a partnership between the Maine Department of Education and Educate Maine/the Teach Maine Center, this event brings together the 2026 Maine DOE Annual Summit and the second annual Every Teacher a Leader Conference for three days of collaboration, inspiration, and high-quality learning for Maine's education workforce.

ElevatED will take place at Thomas College, July 29–31, 2026.

  • Day 1 — July 29: The Annual Summit, tailored for school staff, educators, school safety professionals, and building and instructional leaders.
  • Days 2 & 3 — July 30–31: The Every Teacher a Leader Conference, featuring teacher-led sessions designed specifically for classroom teachers.

Attendees may register for one or both opportunities. Spots are limited and will be granted on a first-come, first-served basis.

Register & Learn More

  • Recap of the 2026 Annual Summit

About the Annual Summit

In 2022, the Maine Department of Education created the Annual Summit to promote its vision for Maine education:

Workforce & Learning
  • A vibrant and respected educator workforce that innovates, leads, and inspires.
  • Learning environments that are safe and supportive for all.
Student Success
  • A pathway to success in school and life for every student.
  • Schools that foster the potential for all to lead purposeful lives.
Community & Civic Life
  • Schools as trusted centers of the community that foster meaningful civic participation and propel Maine's economy.

We thoughtfully and strategically add components each year to bring more support and information to our educators and partners, with the whole student's needs at the forefront. Allowing adequate time and space for collaboration among attendees is a high priority. This valuable exchange creates a community of support that follows attendees throughout the academic year. Many presentations serve as the launch of continued support offered through the Maine DOE.

What Attendees Are Saying

"First and foremost, thank you for your hard work and dedication to the ME Educator Summit! I attended the Safety Summit last year in Windham, but WOW, am I glad I had the opportunity to attend the Educator Summit with the Safety Summit combined. It was GREAT! The inclusion that happened made my typical black sheep of education and transportation department heart, nothing less than full and happy! So again, THANK YOU!"

"As we enter the final day of the Education Summit, I want to thank you for all of your hard work in getting everyone together. I am well aware of how much work this entails behind the scenes, and the speakers, presentations, and networking have been incredibly impressive. Thank you for making the State of Maine a leader in school safety."

"I just wanted to express how much I enjoyed the summit. I hadn't been to an in-person conference since before COVID-19, and it was so nice to see and have actual conversations with so many educators. I feel like I have rediscovered my 'why' for being an educator, and now more than ever, I feel ready to put forth the energy needed to lessen these gaps. Thank you for that!"

decisions.label: Let very uneven cards find their own height
decisions.why: 1 row pairs a short card with one holding nearly three times as much. Equal heights stretch the short one and the difference reads as a hole, so these are allowed to sit at the height of what is in them.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 3 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 3 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Add a contents list (4 sections)
decisions.why: Built from the section headings already on the page. Below three sections a list is not a route.
